critical_code_review_comments: /app/backend/routes/provider_outreach.py PROVIDER_CATALOG is hard-coded in code (14 entries). Fine for v1 launch but the file mixes data (long body_md strings) with logic (the router). At ~280 lines of catalog before any code, consider splitting catalog into /app/backend/routes/_provider_catalog.py so the router file stays slim and adding/editing copy doesn't risk touching endpoint logic.

POST /send writes records inside the loop — if Resend.send raises for provider #3, providers #1 and #2 already have 'sent' rows persisted but #3 has 'error' and #4..N never get attempted. Consider try/except around the entire batch with a per-provider continue (current code already does per-provider try/except — verified — but the dry-run path inserts BEFORE building results, which is fine; just noting batch-failure semantics are correct).

PUT /{id}/status uses Dict[str, Any] payload instead of a Pydantic model — works but bypasses request-shape validation; consider StatusUpdateIn(BaseModel) with Literal['replied','closed','sent','error','dry_run'].
ProviderOutreach.jsx imports `api` as named export — confirmed correct (lib/api.js exports named `api`). Good catch by main agent; many sibling pages still use default import.

BOL fallback path in server.py download_document_pdf: on build_bol_pdf exception, falls back to _build_pdf which is the OLD (now brand-aware) builder. That's correct, but no observability — add logger.warning with the failed document_id so silent fallbacks surface in logs.

Documents BOL data on DOC-FAA5C8A6 still has shipper='Tennant Company' (legacy seed data). The header is now Orisei but the body shipper field reflects original document data — NOT a bug, expected behavior since the doc.data is preserved. If desired, add a migration to rename Tennant shipper to Orisei on seed docs.
